in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to understand your situation. 

**Do you have a child (or children) you're claiming for?** If yes, I'll need to know:

1. **How old is your child (or each child)?** Their age is important as it affects eligibility:
   - Children under 16 generally qualify automatically (with some conditions)
   - Young people aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
   - Those aged 20 or over generally don't qualify

Please tell me about your child or children - their names and ages would be helpful so I can assess each one properly.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'd like to claim for my son Alex. He's 19 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex, who is 19 years old and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 19 (which falls in the 16-19 age category), his eligibility depends on whether he meets certain education or training requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to understand Alex's current situation regarding education or training:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training?** (such as full-time non-advanced education at school or college, or approved unpaid training)
2. **Recently left education or training?** (within the last 20 weeks)
3. **Neither** - not in education/training and left more than 20 weeks ago?

Which of these applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not in college or anything like that anymore. He actually started an apprenticeship recently up in Scotland - he's training in Dundee.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful information! An apprenticeship can count as approved training for Child Benefit purposes.

Let me clarify a few important details about Alex's apprenticeship:

1. **Is this apprenticeship unpaid**, or is he receiving wages/salary for it? This is important because:
   - **Unpaid training/apprenticeships** can qualify for Child Benefit (for 16-19 year olds)
   - **Paid apprenticeships** where he's earning a wage may not qualify, as they're considered employment

2. Also, when did he start this apprenticeship? Is it recent enough that he might still be within 20 weeks of leaving his previous education?

Could you tell me whether Alex is being paid for his apprenticeship, and roughly when he started it?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He is being paid for it - it's a proper apprenticeship with a wage. He started it a few months ago.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important detail.

Since Alex is doing a **paid apprenticeship** (earning a wage), this is generally considered employment rather than unpaid approved training. For Child Benefit purposes, young people aged 16-19 need to be in **approved unpaid training** or **full-time non-advanced education** to qualify.

Let me ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

1. **When exactly did Alex finish his previous education** (school or college)? I need to know if he left within the last 20 weeks, as there can be an extension period that covers the gap between leaving education and turning 20.

2. **When will Alex turn 20?** Child Benefit eligibility ends at age 20 for young people in this category, even if they meet other criteria.

These details will help me determine if there's any extension period that might apply to Alex's situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school last year, so it's been well over 20 weeks. And he'll be turning 20 in a few months' time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Let me complete the assessment based on what you've told me about Alex.

conversation.text:
## Assessment Result: **Not Eligible**

I'm sorry, but based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Why Alex doesn't qualify:

**Alex is 19 years old**, which means he falls into the 16-19 age category where Child Benefit can continue - but only under specific circumstances:

- Young people aged 16-19 must be in **approved unpaid training** or **full-time non-advanced education** to qualify
- Since Alex is doing a **paid apprenticeship**, this is considered employment rather than approved unpaid training
- He's not currently in full-time education
- He left school over 20 weeks ago, so the extension period (which can apply for up to 20 weeks after leaving education) no longer applies

### Important to know:

- Child Benefit for young people in this age group stops completely when they turn **20**, regardless of their circumstances
- If Alex were in an **unpaid** apprenticeship or training program, or if he were in full-time college education (at a non-advanced level), he would qualify

### What this means:

Even though Alex is still living at home with you and is only 19, his paid apprenticeship status means he doesn't meet the qualifying criteria for Child Benefit.

If you have any questions about this decision or if Alex's circumstances change (for example, if he returns to full-time education), please feel free to reach out to the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.
